_comment: THE AGENTIC HARNESS layer. Owner, 2026-09-20: "cat-harness, folio-assistant-core, folio-assistant are distinct instances/schemas" — so this declares itself `cat-harness` rather than `folio-assistant`. It carried the latter until the repository root gained a harness.json of its own, at which point TWO instances declared one name and `instanceRoots` — keyed on the declared name — could only hold one of them. The one it held was the root, so `folio-assistant` resolved to the checkout and the harness layer became unreachable by name. `stub` is UNCHANGED and stays `folio-assistant`: the stub names the PUBLISHED artefact (docs/folio-assistant/, _kg/folio-assistant.jsonld, the Pages path) and the name names the instance, which is the entire reason a declaration carries both. The CatHarness declaration for THIS instance — what directories it scans and what kind of graph each holds. See skills/folio-core/directory-conventions.md. This repo is PRE-SPLIT (issue #223), so it declares what is true today, not the target layout: `tools/` and `folio/` do not exist here yet and are deliberately not declared. A directory that is declared but absent is worse than one that is missing, because every consumer then scans nothing and reports a clean run over it. NOTE: `schemas/` declares TWO graphs — the first real use of the array. A directory is a place to look and may hold more than one part of the graph; it does not say how to tell them apart, because the files declare what they are (see bean xxxb: schemas/*.ts does not yet do this well). `beans/` is declared ONCE, as a single `beans` graph. Its internal split — `defs` for work items, `workflows` for running BPMN state — is declared by `beans/beans.json`, not here. #263 declared the two as separate directories, one nested inside the other, which left a consumer unable to tell which owned what beneath it; the nodes now carry that.
_title: No `title`, deliberately: `displayTitle` is title || name || id, so the sidebar and the landing page fall back to `name` — which the schema already requires to be the instance's identifier, the one artefacts are stub-named after. A title here said `c@t-harness` and overrode that, labelling THIS repository with the brand of the harness layer that is still to be split out of it. Setting the title to `folio-assistant` instead would be the same fact in two fields, free to drift. The c@t-harness derivation stays in the description, where it is a tagline rather than an identity.
name: cat-harness
_title_comment: THE PUBLISHED SITE'S TITLE, stated rather than inherited. `sync-docs-harness` renders `title ?? name` into `docs/_data/harness.json`, which just-the-docs draws at the top of every page's sidebar — so while this instance was NAMED `folio-assistant` the fallback happened to give the right answer. Renaming it to `cat-harness` on the owner's 2026-09-20 ruling retitled the whole published site, which is a user-visible change nobody asked for and which no test would have caught. The site's title is its PUBLISHED identity, the same fact `stub` carries; the name is the instance's.

assets.title: AGENTS.md — folio-assistant
assets.description: The file every cold agent reads first, and until 2026-09-19 the ONLY root artefact this instance did not declare — `directories[]` and `images[]` carried everything else. Bean `v8gh` is what that cost: seven dead links, five broken by one directory move, including the one its own banner calls the place to start, so an agent following the banner hit a 404. Nothing caught them; `readme:audit` checks README.md alone and `check:agents-xref` checks citations INTO this file rather than links out of it. `source` names the cat-bootstrap instance it descends from, so "is this still what it was copied from" is a question that can be ASKED — 'it was copied at init' is not an answer.

assets.title: folio-assistant
assets.description: The reader-facing entry point. Its generated sections are written by `readme:sync` only where the file already carries their markers, and `readme:audit` verifies every other link.

assets.title: Initializing into folio-assistant
assets.description: What cat-bootstrap's step 2 reads once it has been pointed at THIS instance. Published at the fixed convention every cat-harness instance honours, composed by `initializationDoc()` rather than spelled, so cat-bootstrap needs no per-target knowledge and can initialise into a SPECIALISED harness it was never written against. Declared as an asset as well as conventional, so `check:declared-assets` verifies it is there and that its links resolve: a convention nothing checks is a convention that is honoured until it quietly is not. The path is INSTANCE-relative here, not `<stub>/docs/...`: this instance has its own directory (`cat-harness/`), so `siteDir` is plain `docs`, and the stub names published artefacts rather than a directory. Whether cat-bootstrap can still find it from one reference is open — see bean `wggr`.

_publication_comment: The `publication host` axis of docs/proposals/deployment-topologies.md, accepted 2026-09-19 (issue #363). WHAT KIND of host serves the renderings — distinct from `canonicalUrl` (the base @ids are minted against) and from `readme.linkStyle` in harness.config.json (how a link to a published artefact is written). This instance really does publish to GitHub Pages, so it declares so; an instance that has not said is `undefined`, which is a third state and must never be read as `github-pages`.

stickies._comment: ONE CARD FOR THIS HARNESS, per the owner's ruling of 2026-09-20: "not all stickies should be cat harness they should be outputs (as if) each init harness ran ... each own intiaization sticky note to show sucess". It replaces three — `landing`, `cat-harness` and `subgraphs`. The first two are merged here because they were always this one harness talking about itself twice; the third moved to folio-assist-core, whose subject content IS.  `bodyFrom: description` rather than a literal body, so the c@t-harness derivation chain is read from the declaration above and cannot drift from it — the owner: "dont lose acronym definitions". `bodyAppend` carries the cat's introduction and the scope line, which is why that field exists.  THEME `grumpy-cat`, the sage hoodie, per "cat-harness=gumpy hoddie".
stickies.summary: computable adjudication and agentic test harness
stickies.bodyAppend:
Please be introduced to a cat who acquires things, for whatever purpose — maybe somebody knows.

**Scope:** the platform — skills, schemas, processes, the MCP server and the pipeline. Not what a folio IS (that is folio-assist-core), and not any folio's own content, which lives in its own repository.

links.label: cat-harness, in the source
links.note: Still to be split out of this repository — issue #223.

links.label: RTFM — the cat-harness docs
links.note: The agent–user interaction model, and what this harness is for.

directories.description: Tool definitions, one subdirectory per contributing instance (tools/<stub>/) so a composed instance adds its own without colliding on a filename. tools/index.ts merges them and is the only path a consumer imports. Authored as .ts calling defineTool so a malformed node fails at tsc; the JSON-LD and JSON Schema renderings are generated.

The content-object model and the per-skill JSON Schemas. Declares BOTH graphs: the schema definitions themselves, and `kg` because a schema IS a knowledge-graph node — the .ts files are part of the KG, not a separate island beside it.

The cat-bootstrap graph's SKILLS — what an agent reads before it knows whether this repository is an instance, what kind, or what for. A SECOND `cat-harness` directory beside `skills/`, and the first real use of the topical layout the declaration was built for: `kgRoots()` returns two, and every consumer reading the declaration rather than the literal `skills/` finds both with no code change. IT POINTS AT `cat-bootstrap/skills/`, NOT `cat-bootstrap/`, and the one level matters. `isSkillMd` is declaration-over-location: a markdown file that does not declare `$schema:` IS a skill. `cat-bootstrap/README.md` and `cat-bootstrap/AGENTS.md` declare neither, and they are the cat-bootstrap instance's two DECLARED ASSETS — so a graph rooted at `cat-bootstrap/` counts them as skill nodes and the scan contradicts a declaration that has already answered the question. Measured on this branch before the fix: `skill/AGENTS` was in the export. #422 found this from the other side and declared `skills/` inside `cat-bootstrap/harness.json`; this entry is the same fact at the root, and it is stated twice BY DECISION (2026-09-20) rather than by necessity. THE EARLIER NOTE HERE WAS WRONG and the correction is the useful part: it said "this instance depends on cat-bootstrap" is not expressible because `HarnessConfigDependenciesSchema` knows only `folioAssistant`. That key does not mean the folio-assistant PACKAGE — its own doc comment reads "Other folio-assistant instances this folio depends on", and cat-bootstrap is such an instance by every test the code applies. MEASURED, not argued: writing `cat-harness/harness.config.json` with `{name: "cat-bootstrap", path: "../cat-bootstrap", provides: ["skills"]}` serves cat-bootstrap through `LOCAL_PACKAGES` with `folio-assistant` unmoved. The zod schema needs no change at all. WHAT ACTUALLY BLOCKS IT is one directory entry, and it is not in the dependency schema: cat-bootstrap declares `workflows/` with no `scope`, so cat-harness INHERITS it, and `materialiseDirectories` resolves an inherited path against the INHERITING instance by design — it wants `cat-harness/workflows/`, which does not exist, and `harness:dirs:check` reports `21 declared, 1 missing` and exits 1. The gap it exposes is general and this entry is only where it surfaced: a `ContentDirectory` cannot say whether it is a LAYOUT dependents should reproduce (`uploads/`, `library/`, `voices/`) or merely WHERE ITS OWN CONTENT LIVES (`workflows/`, `schemas/`, `tools/`). Simulated on a fresh folio depending on this instance, `init-folio` would create five directories it has no use for, each with a committed keep-marker — the `dh4f` shape, shipped downstream. Adding that distinction was considered and DECLINED for now: it is a schema change whose per-directory classification is a judgement about every directory here, not a cat-bootstrap workaround. So THIS entry stays, and the thing to fix before deleting it is the convention/content distinction — not the dependency schema. The earlier note here said `resolveSkillDirs` had no caller: it has one — `discoverLocalPackages` — and the reachability it was waiting on arrived with the `scope` fix in `ownDirectories`, which until then resolved this path against the INSTANCE and so dropped it for not existing. REPOSITORY-scoped: it sits at the top of the checkout, not inside this instance, and it is deliberately never overlaid by a dependency.

directories._comment: CAT-BOOTSTRAP'S RENDER SUBGRAPH, declared here for the same reason its sibling above is: `resolveSkillDirs` walks THIS instance's declaration plus its dependencies, and cat-bootstrap is not a declared dependency of cat-harness — it is composed under it. So a directory declared only in `cat-bootstrap/harness.json` is invisible to `skill_fetch` from this root, which is how cat-bootstrap's own skills came to be declared twice BY DECISION (see the entry above). WITHOUT IT the two skills that constitute cat-bootstrap's rendering exemption are unfetchable from the root — and an exemption whose substitute cannot be reached is the hole `renderExemption.owes` exists to close. Bean `hfkl`. A SEPARATE id from `cat-bootstrap`, because overrides match on id and reusing it would replace the skills with these.

directories.description: The knowledge graph. Skill packages, and the four other node kinds that point at them: `roles/roles.json` (a role IS a BPMN swimlane, and carries the skills its lane's activities need), `workflows/*.bpmn` + `workflows/decisions/*.dmn` (the processes those roles act in, reached through the skill that describes them), `requirements/*.json` (conformance obligations whose `satisfiedBy` names the skill or capability discharging them), `permissions/permissions.json` (what an actor may DO in any lane, as opposed to what its lane's role knows), Its audit verdicts are NOT here: they moved to the `qa` tree on 2026-09-19, because a verdict is a QA reviewer's output and placement follows provenance. Note the id is `kg` while the path is `skills/` — ids are stable across a relocation, paths are not.

RACI as its own subgraph beside CRDM. Three declared edge kinds — accountable, consulted, informed — over the BPMN activities and `roles.json` entries that already exist, NOT a new party registry: a second table of names would be a second answer to `who is the reviewer`, free to disagree with the registry, which is the drift the retired skill `roles:` field cost 260 dangling values (bean qif9). R is deliberately absent because a lane already declares it. Owner, 2026-09-20, bean 7o7i: exactly one Accountable per activity, ENFORCED by `check:raci`.

CRDM as its OWN topical subgraph — its skills and its eight diagrams together, rather than three skills in folio-core and eight .bpmn in skills/workflows/ with nothing but a filename prefix relating them. Owner, 2026-09-20: CRDM, RACI, SDLC and MADR all live under `methodologies/`, each its own subgraph. I proposed a separate `workflow-methodologies/` on the reading that PROCESS methods (how a process runs) and JUDGEMENT methods (how to decide — Kepner-Tregoe, MADR, DMN) are different axes; the owner settled it as ONE tree, which is the better answer for the reason this repository keeps relearning: two directories whose boundary needs a paragraph to explain are two answers to `where do methodologies live`, and the next author picks the wrong one. This is the layout `skillMdDirs` was built for: its own comment names `crdm` as the example of a topical directory that should cost a declaration line and no code change, and `cat-bootstrap/skills/` was the first such root. Each methodology is declared SEPARATELY rather than declaring the parent, because `workflowDirs` resolves `<kgdir>/workflows` — declaring only the parent would leave every diagram undiscovered. SDLC and RACI are deliberately NOT declared until they have content: a declared-but-absent directory is the `dh4f` defect.

Judgement methodologies the harness owns, one sub-graph each: Kepner-Tregoe for a decision, MADR for its record, DMN for the computable case. PARALLEL rather than composable — which applies is contextual, and blending them produces a house method that cites nobody. Its own graph kind rather than skills, for three properties a skill does not have: extractable (somebody else's work, adopted, so it lifts out with its declaration when the field moves on), referenced rather than inlined (two skills quoting one method is two copies free to drift), and exempt from skill criteria (skill-is-brief caps an INSTRUCTION near 280 lines; a methodology is a faithful rendering of an external standard, and truncating it to fit a house limit would misrepresent the standard). GRADE is deliberately NOT here — see smart-kg-methodologies.

Everything a QA process produced, in one declared tree. The owner's rule, 2026-09-19: an artefact generated primarily as a QA reviewer belongs under `test/results/` as part of a QA process — placement follows PROVENANCE, not file family and not who fetches it afterwards. Three kinds live here and the FILES say which they are, per the `$schema` contract: `qa-results/v1` (`<producer>.qa-results.json`, a whole-artefact review — findings about a document the build just produced), `qa-witness/v1` (`witnesses/**`, one per audited subject in the families `block`, `kg` and `translation`, the published projection) and `kg-qa/v1` (`kg-qa/**`, the KG verdicts themselves — what `kg-audit` wrote). The `kg-qa/` tree MIRRORS each subject's path rather than being flat, and that is not tidiness: measured 2026-09-19, four sidecar basenames already occur twice across packages (`editor`, `getting-started`, `idle-backlog`, `l2-dak-authoring`), so a flat directory would silently overwrite four verdicts. `kgQaSidecarPath` in `schemas/kg-qa.ts` is the one answer for writer and reader alike. A directory is a PLACE TO LOOK and may hold more than one part of a graph; extension is a coincidence, a declaration inside the file is the contract. ONE entry rather than a nested set, deliberately: #263's own comment names the defect a declaration inside another declaration creates. STILL OUTSIDE: the 122 block verdicts `*.qa.json`, which sit beside their blocks and move next. The witnesses are PUBLISHED at `/assets/qa/`, which is where every badge points; the publishing workflows copy them into `_site/assets/qa/` after Jekyll, since Jekyll builds only `docs/`. The trashcan that is kept. Deprecated and throwaway structured content — addressable, exported as <base>/fsh-guts.jsonld, and DELIBERATELY absent from the rendered site. Every other declared kind here is non-renderable because it is a graph a tool reads and there was never a page to make of it; this one's contents could be rendered and are not, so that something can be kept without being published. It is also the destination that makes the never-delete rule enforceable beyond beans: AGENTS.md forbids deleting a bean because a scrapped item stops the next agent re-entering a dead end while a deleted one cannot be told from an accident, and that reasoning was always general — an agent removing a page or a script had only `rm`. Delete now means relocate here, and relocate is reversible. Files declare themselves with `$schema: folio-fsh-guts/v1`, per the same contract the bean and workflow stores use. Repository health reports — what the daily sweep under `test/health/` wrote. The owner settled it on `test/` the same day and it moved as its own change — bean `auap`, PR #400. The `id` here is unchanged, deliberately: an inheriting instance overrides on the entry's id and never on its path, so `health` still binds after the relocation. The e2e specs came to the declaration rather than the declaration to the specs, because `testDir` is one line of one config file and a declared path is what every downstream override resolves against.

The work plan. `beans/beans.json` declares its nodes — `defs` (work items) and `workflows` (running BPMN instance state). REPOSITORY-scoped: it sits at the top of the checkout, not inside this instance, and it is deliberately never overlaid by a dependency.

The incoming queue of the document-ingestion pipeline — raw files as dropped, before ingestion.
